signals.signal: Investor Update (03/03/2026) discloses cumulative IT OPEX of c.EUR 175m for 2023-2025 rising to c.EUR 240m for 2026-2028 (+37%), earmarked for automation/centralisation, infrastructure modernisation and system upgrades, migration of data to multi-cloud platforms and a composable microservices architecture already underway; C/I target c.40% for 2026-2028.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus Investor Update presentation (slide 53)
signals.implies: A named, quantified three-year IT spend envelope with explicit modernisation/automation lines - the budget line Printec managed services, self-service software and AML/monitoring would be funded from.
signals.likelihood: High - budget already committed in guidance
signals.followup: Ask IR for the split of the c.EUR 240m between core, channels and cash automation; check 4 Aug H1-2026 deck for a first-half IT opex actual.

signals.signal: Cash 360 real-time notes-and-coins business deposit machines shrank from 22 locations (list dated 12/07/2024) to 5 locations (list dated 01/12/2025), all of them unmanned mall sites. In-branch business cash deposit is instead served by 32 envelope-based Pay-In (BCS) machines and 30 coin-deposit machines (both lists dated 09/06/2026).
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus deposit-machine location lists (Cash 360, Pay-In BCS, Coin Deposit PDFs)
signals.implies: Real-time cash acceptance pulled back to 5 unmanned sites while 32 branch locations still rely on envelope deposits needing manual back-office counting - a direct opening for cash recyclers / smart-deposit units and cash-cycle managed services.
signals.followup: Identify the OEM behind Cash 360 and BCS units (Glory hypothesis unproven).

signals.signal: Investor Update quantifies the estate downsizing: branches 108 (Jan-2019) to 56 (Dec-2025), -48%; employees 4,146 to 2,850, -31%; active digital users 281k to 504k, +79%; 2025 targeted Voluntary Exit Plan cost EUR 19m for c.110 leavers, 2.3-year payback (EUR 14m booked 4Q2025).
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus Investor Update presentation (slide 52)
signals.implies: Halved branch count with rising digital volume forces per-branch throughput up - trigger for teller-cash automation, assisted self-service and remote/video servicing.
signals.followup: Confirm branch count at 30/06/2026 in the 4 Aug H1 deck.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Cyprus / Cyprus market
signals.signal: CBC Payment Statistics H2-2025 (released 22/07/2026) puts the total ATM estate in Cyprus at 396 at end-H2-2025, down from 398 a year earlier and down c.13% over five years; c.73% of Cyprus ATMs are contactless vs a 38% euro-area average; EUR 2.6bn was withdrawn from ATMs in H2-2025 and the average withdrawal hit a record EUR 390 (vs EUR 307 in H2-2022, +27%); over-the-counter cash withdrawals have almost halved in three years. The CBC explicitly warns that further changes in the total ATM count are expected 'within the coming months as the institutions reassess and rationalise their ATM networks' after the two 2025 systemic acquisitions.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus, Statistical Release - Payment Statistics: second half of 2025 (PDF)
signals.implies: The regulator itself forecasts an imminent island-wide ATM rationalisation - the exact moment to sell fleet consolidation, ATM-as-a-service / managed services, recyclers that cut CIT cost per unit, and branch-cash automation as the OTC replacement. Fewer but far busier ATMs (record average withdrawal) argues for higher-capacity recycling machines rather than cash-out-only units.
signals.likelihood: High - CBC states the reassessment is already under way
signals.followup: Ask BOC and Eurobank Cyprus which sites are on the rationalisation list and whether they will outsource rather than replace; pitch a managed-ATM commercial model.

signals.signal: The live New Branch Model page confirms the reformatted estate: 29 full-service branches, 12 lending units, 15 transaction branches, 5 unmanned Digital Branches and 17 extended-hours self-service points. Transaction branches and digital branches run on self-service machines only (coin and banknote deposit), for authorised legal entities, 7 days a week 08:00-22:00, with card-controlled access. Digital branches are explicitly described as 'unmanned operating branches'.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus - New Branch Model (bank website)
signals.implies: 32 of 56 sites (15 transaction + 5 digital + 12 lending) already run with no or minimal teller cash - a fully-formed self-service branch estate that needs device monitoring, remote management, incident/SLA managed services, cash forecasting and CIT optimisation, plus assisted-service and video-banking add-ons. Printec's managed-services and cash-automation lines map directly.
signals.followup: Establish who monitors and services the machines at the 5 unmanned digital branches today and when that contract renews.

signals.signal: 1Q2026 results (11/05/2026): cost-to-income 37%, total operating expenses EUR 91m of which staff costs EUR 48m; opex down 20% qoq purely because the c.EUR 14m VEP charge fell out of 4Q2025 (c.110 leavers); 508k active users of digital channels at 31/03/2026; profit after tax EUR 121m; NPE ratio 1.1%. The bank also agreed to buy a c.EUR 150m performing loan and c.EUR 500m deposit portfolio from CDB Bank, completion expected by end-2026.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus Group 1Q2026 Financial Results presentation (PDF)
signals.implies: Cost discipline is delivered by headcount, not yet by channel automation - the remaining lever is per-transaction cost in branches. The CDB portfolio adds corporate/SME customers (and their cash and card volumes) without adding branches, increasing pressure on self-service throughput and on onboarding/eKYC and AML screening capacity.
signals.followup: Position eKYC/onboarding and AML screening capacity for the CDB customer migration ahead of end-2026 completion.

signals.signal: A further targeted Voluntary Exit Plan was opened in early June 2026 for c.40 staff, restricted to employees with more than 25 years' service in the Group or aged over 55, with a maximum ex-gratia compensation of EUR 200,000 and extra incentives for those over 60; it closed on 19/06/2026.
signals.source_name: Offsite.com.cy / 24h.com.cy (Cyprus press) on the Bank of Cyprus targeted VEP
signals.implies: A second, smaller exit wave inside 8 months signals continuing branch-role removal; every teller taken out has to be replaced by a machine or a digital journey. Supports recycler/assisted-service and video-banking propositions.
signals.followup: Look for the exit-cost line in the 04/08/2026 H1-2026 P&L to size the second VEP; no BOC stock-exchange announcement was found for it.

signals.signal: H1-2026 results: the Board meets on 03/08/2026 to review the six months to 30/06/2026 and to consider an interim dividend; results are published before market open on 04/08/2026 on Euronext Athens and the Cyprus Stock Exchange, with an analysts' briefing the same day. Not yet published as at 30/07/2026.
signals.source_name: Bank of Cyprus Financial Calendar 2026 / Cyprus Mail
signals.implies: A dated, imminent disclosure event: the H1-2026 deck should refresh branch count, headcount, digital users and the exit-cost line, and is the right hook for a follow-up commercial conversation in the week of 04/08/2026.
signals.followup: Re-run this bank on 04-05/08/2026 to capture the H1-2026 estate and IT-cost disclosures.

signals.signal: The Cyprus Tenders Review Authority on 15/07/2026 unanimously rejected all ten grounds of JCC's fifth appeal, definitively awarding the Government's electronic-payments processing contract to VivaBank (successor to Viva Payments Services S.A.), which had the lower/most economically advantageous bid. The tender opened 07/01/2022; the Tenders Board awarded to VivaBank on 20/03/2026 and JCC appealed again on 08/04/2026. The contract runs 67 months in total - a technical integration phase with the 'Ariadne' payment gateway plus 36 months of service, renewable for two further 12-month periods. JCC had held the state e-payments monopoly since 2010.
signals.implies: The Cypriot acquiring monopoly has just been broken at the top of the market. JCC is majority-owned by Bank of Cyprus, so BOC loses processing volume and gains a genuine competitive threat - which usually triggers a terminal/estate and acceptance-platform refresh. Opening for Printec POS/acquiring, terminal management and merchant-services capability on both sides of the fight.
signals.followup: Confirm JCC's exact shareholding split from a primary filing; approach JCC on POS estate modernisation and BOC on merchant-acquiring defence.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Cyprus / Cyprus market
signals.signal: CBC Payment Fraud Statistics H1-2025 (published 16/02/2026) reports fraudulent payment transactions in Cyprus up 30% yoy in volume to c.16,000 and up 66% in value to almost EUR 4m, growing faster than the euro area (c.9m transactions, +6% in value to EUR 1.7bn). Card fraud is 92% of fraud volume but 97% of card fraud is online; 54% of fraud value is credit transfers, of which 59% are manipulation-of-the-payer (authorised push payment) cases; the average value of a fraudulent credit transfer in Cyprus is among the highest in the euro area; cross-border card fraud is c.24x more likely than domestic.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of Cyprus, Statistical Release - Payment Fraud Statistics: first half of 2025 (PDF)
signals.implies: A regulator-published, quantified deterioration in APP/manipulation fraud and online card fraud - the strongest available business case in Cyprus for real-time transaction monitoring, behavioural fraud analytics, Verification of Payee and stronger authentication. Directly addressable by Printec's transaction-monitoring, AML/compliance and HSM/security lines at BOC as the largest issuer.
signals.followup: Watch for the H2-2025 fraud release; pitch APP-fraud/behavioural monitoring to BOC and JCC.

signals.signal: Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Report 2025-2026 figures: Bank of Cyprus 56 branches, 132 ATMs, 2,447 employees; sector totals across the 8 remaining member banks 155 branches, 321 ATMs, 6,253 employees (vs 384 / 423 / 9,273 across 12 banks in 2013). Eurobank (ex-Hellenic) is now larger by network at 59 branches and 156 ATMs.
signals.source_name: CBN Cyprus Business News, citing Association of Cyprus Banks Annual Report 2025-2026
signals.implies: ACB member banks account for only 321 of the 396 ATMs the CBC counts in Cyprus, implying roughly 75 machines run by non-ACB operators (independent deployers / co-operative and payment institutions) - an addressable independent-ATM segment alongside the bank fleets. BOC at 132 ATMs across 56 sites is now the number-two network by ATMs.
signals.likelihood: Medium - the residual is derived, not disclosed
signals.followup: Obtain the ACB Annual Report 2025-2026 PDF directly to verify, and identify who operates the c.75 non-ACB ATMs.

signals.signal: Jinius, the Bank of Cyprus Group digital platform, provides the Invoice Management Service through which businesses send electronic invoices to the Cypriot government; all ministries, several municipalities and EOA have adopted it, and electronically submitted invoices are prioritised for payment within 20 days.
signals.source_name: Cyprus Mail / Jinius Business (Bank of Cyprus Group)
signals.implies: BOC owns the de-facto national B2G e-invoicing rail, which pulls SME transaction and payment data into the group. Adjacent Printec opportunities: digital onboarding/eKYC for platform merchants, payment-initiation and POS bundling, and AML/KYC screening on the merchant base.
signals.followup: Check whether Cyprus mandates B2B e-invoicing (ViDA timetable) and whether Jinius will need third-party KYC/AML tooling at scale.

signals.signal: Printec (Cyprus) Ltd, founded 1995 with 17 employees and 60+ customers, publishes an installed base of 26,000+ POS terminals under management, 152 self-service kiosks and 128 teller cash recyclers, and carries a named testimonial from Panicos Athanasiades, Manager Consumer Banking Systems & Operations, Bank of Cyprus: the partnership has been 'instrumental in transforming our branches', advancing digitalisation while 'maintaining seamless access to cash services'. Printec's portfolio page also lists a Bank of Cyprus teller-cash-recycler case study.
signals.source_name: Printec Group - Printec Cyprus country page
signals.implies: Confirms Printec as the incumbent branch-transformation and cash-automation integrator at Bank of Cyprus, and sizes the Cyprus TCR base at 128 units. The incumbency is the platform for extending into the 32 envelope-based Pay-In sites, the 5 unmanned digital branches, ATM managed services and the compliance/fraud suite. The TCR OEM behind the 128 units is still not named publicly.
signals.followup: Get the internal split of the 128 TCRs by bank and confirm the OEM; use the Athanasiades relationship to bid the Pay-In envelope replacement and the H1-2026 ATM rationalisation.

signals.signal: QuickHub is marketed as BOC's 'next-gen digital branch', but is delivered entirely inside the BoC Mobile App and Internet Banking - account opening, credit card issuance, personal loan and car hire-purchase applications, car and home insurance, and in-app cheque deposit. It is not a physical kiosk estate.
signals.implies: BOC's 'digital branch' strategy is app-first, so remote account opening at volume needs industrial-grade identity verification - a direct fit for Printec's identity-based digital services / eKYC and for AML screening at onboarding. Conversely it confirms there is no in-branch assisted-service kiosk layer yet, which is a white space.
signals.followup: Ask who supplies BOC's remote identity verification today and whether in-branch assisted kiosks are on the 2026-2028 roadmap.

coverage_notes: Resumed from checkpoint (3 signals carried unchanged from the interrupted run of the same runDate) and completed the gaps its 'remaining' note listed. Angles worked this run, in English and Greek: (1) BOC's own site - New Branch Model, ATM page, QuickHub, deposit-machine pages (EN and GR trees); (2) BOC investor materials - 1Q2026 results presentation PDF downloaded and text-extracted locally, 2026 financial calendar; (3) Central Bank of Cyprus statistical releases - Payment Statistics H2-2025 and Payment Fraud Statistics H1-2025, both PDFs downloaded with a desktop User-Agent and parsed with pdfminer; (4) ECB payments statistics release for euro-area comparators; (5) Greek-language Cypriot press (offsite.com.cy, 24h.com.cy, inbusinessnews/reporter.com.cy, stockwatch, politis, alphanews) on the June-2026 VEP and the JCC/VivaBank tender; (6) vendor-side sources - Printec Group country and solutions pages, fetched with a desktop UA after 403s; (7) Association of Cyprus Banks 2025-2026 network figures via CBN. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the carried baseline: the CBC H2-2025 payment-statistics PDF is NOT corrupt - it downloads and extracts cleanly with a desktop User-Agent plus pdfminer, and gives 396 ATMs in Cyprus at end-H2-2025 versus 398 at end-H2-2024. The previously carried '405 ATMs at end-H1-2025' should be retired in favour of 396. GENUINE GAPS: (a) the TCR / deposit-machine OEM at Bank of Cyprus remains unidentified - Printec is confirmed as the integrator and quotes 128 TCRs across its Cyprus base, but no OEM is named on Printec's Cyprus page and its partners page carries no extractable brand logos, so the 'Glory incumbency' in the brief stays UNPROVEN and is not reported as fact; (b) BOC does not publish its own ATM count anywhere on its site - the 132 figure is press-relayed from the ACB Annual Report 2025-2026 and the ACB's own publications page still lists 2023-2024 as its latest, so that row is Low confidence; (c) H1-2026 results are not published until 04/08/2026, so no half-year estate, headcount or IT-cost actuals exist yet - a re-run in the week of 4 August is required; (d) no CBC AML enforcement action against Bank of Cyprus was found in 2026; (e) JCC's precise shareholding percentages could not be verified from a primary filing (jcc.com.cy/about-us returns 404) - only aggregator claims of a Bank of Cyprus controlling stake, so no percentage is asserted; (f) Jinius's 2026 activity beyond the October-2025 public-sector e-invoicing adoption was not found.
